title: Pruning playbook & UX triage notes — Sprint 27
content:
Purpose:
- Create a lightweight, repeatable playbook for pruning and triaging console & tooling backlog items ahead of Sprint 27 kickoff.
- Capture quick UX wireframe notes for any tickets we decide to carry forward so engineering has a minimal spec.
- Drive consistent decisions: what stays, what gets deferred to parking lot, what needs a follow-up spike.

Scope:
- Applies to tickets currently in console-and-rollouts inbox + long-tail 'tooling' tickets older than 60 days.
- Focus: Console UX surface (routes, rollout UI, model selection, per-route dashboards) and dev-facing tooling (route config builder, rollout policies).
- Out of scope: infra-only SRE requests, Dedicated infra capacity planning (pass to eng-infra).

Quick heuristics for triage decisions (use as checklist):
1) Customer impact: blocking customers or tied to enterprise contract? (Yes -> keep)
2) Product funnel impact: will this materially improve time-to-value or retention?
3) Effort estimate: <3d, 3-10d, >10d (if >10d need PM sign-off and likely split).
4) Risk/exposure: security/compliance/regulatory? (high risk -> escalate)
5) Age & duplication: duplicate or abandoned >60 days -> consider prune.

Decision buckets (examples):
- Keep / sprint-ready (green): clear ACs, <10d, high impact or contractual.
- Keep / needs spike (amber): unknown perf/regression risk, requires 1-3 day spike to size work.
- Defer / parking lot (blue): nice-to-have, low impact, no customer ask.
- Prune / close (red): stale, duplicate, low ROI after discussion.

Pruning rules (must apply all when considering close):
- No active collaborator or customer request in the last 90 days.
- Overlaps with existing shipped feature or roadmap item (link PR/epic).
- Small orphan improvements (<2d) that still deliver value should be scheduled rather than closed.
- If a ticket is blocked on external dependency with no ETA, move to parking lot not closed.

Prioritization matrix (quick scoring):
- Impact (1-5) + Effort (1-5) + Risk (1-3) -> raw score = Impact*2 - Effort - Risk.
- Thresholds: score >=6 keep, 3-5 spike/consider, <=2 defer/prune.
- Note: apply qualitative override for contractual/enterprise issues.

Wireframe quick notes (attach to ticket as 'ux-delta' comment):
1) Compact route list (mobile + desktop): tighten row density, show model variant badge, token-cost estimate inline.
   - Wire: icon | route name | model badge | last-deploy | qps | action-menu
   - AC: row height <= 48px on desktop, cost tooltip on hover, accessible labels.
2) Model selection microflow (route-level): preview latency/cost delta before saving.
   - Wire: modal with comparison table: model | avg latency | 95p latency | token cost per 1k
   - AC: preview must not trigger billing events; mock sample outputs OK.
3) Rollout canary control: expose atomic toggles for traffic split + quick rollback.
   - Wire: slider + numeric input; live traffic % preview; last 10 errors sample.
   - AC: must hook to routing policy API; guard for enterprise-only features behind entitlement.
4) Route-level tracing badge: show last 5 traces link (opens tracing console).
   - AC: only show when tracing is enabled; lazy-load to avoid perf hit.

Sample ticket decisions (triage session notes):
- JIRA-4572: "Route model selector: cost preview"
  - Current: no cost preview, PM flagged as frequent ask from Sales during demos.
  - Triage: Keep / sprint-ready.
  - Rationale: Demo blocker, low-medium effort (est. 4d), high impact.
  - Owner: Arjun Patel (PM) to add mock data; UX -> deliver modal wireframe.
  - AC to include: sample token cost calculation for 1k tokens, non-billing preview mode.

- JIRA-4589: "Rollout UX: expose rule builder for canary"
  - Current: backend supports weighted routing but no UI.
  - Triage: Keep / needs spike.
  - Rationale: Potentially >10d if we include audit+entitlements; do a 2d spike to prototype slider and edge cases.
  - Spike outcome: a small prototype with slider component + API contract doc.
  - Owner: Liam O'Neill (PM).

- JIRA-4411: "Compact dashboard: token breakdown per route" (old)
  - Current: ticket created 120 days ago, no recent activity.
  - Triage: Defer / parking lot.
  - Rationale: low request volume; similar capability planned in Optimize roadmap Q1. Link: CON-OPT-ROADMAP-2027.

- JIRA-4622: "Feature flag to hide experimental buttons"
  - Triage: Prune / close (red).
  - Rationale: feature flagged experimental buttons are not shipped; owners moved on; re-open if ask resurfaces.

Acceptance criteria template for 'keep' items (add to ticket):
- Context: short one-liner of customer/PM ask.
- UX: attach 1–2 wireframe PNGs + alt text describing interactions.
- Backend contract: list of endpoints/fields touched and expected shape.
- Test plan: manual test checklist + 1 automated integration test scenario.
- Rollout plan: canary percentage steps + rollback criteria.

Developer handoff checklist (add comment when moving to In Progress):
- [ ] Wireframe attached and labelled with screens and states.
- [ ] API contract documented (endpoint + sample payloads).
- [ ] Perf/regression risk flagged if >50ms expected latency change.
- [ ] QA smoke steps documented.

Ops & release notes blurb (short templates):
- For rollout-related UX changes: "Added route-level model cost preview and canary slider. Admins can now preview cost differences before saving; canary traffic controls exposed in route settings (requires entitlements)."
- For small UX polish: "Adjusted row density in Routes list to improve scanability on small displays."

Meeting cadence & owners for pruning:
- Weekly groom + prune sync: Mon 10:00 (30m) — product-console + 1 eng rep (rotate).
- Deep-prune session: sprint planning day (90m) — include SRE if tickets touch tracing or infra.
- Owner for next prune: Maya Chen (rotate to Sofia for Sprint 28).

Next steps (this doc):
- Arjun: add mocks for JIRA-4572 by 2026-09-14.
- Liam: run 2d spike for JIRA-4589 and publish notes to linked Confluence page by 2026-09-16.
- Maya: run prune sweep on tickets older than 90 days and prepare PR list for closures by 2026-09-15.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we surface estimated token-costs for embeddings vs. generation in the same UI? (UX trade-offs).
- Confirm entitlement gating model with security for rollout audit logs (SRE + security).
- Decide default row density for compact mode vs. default mode (A/B test?).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep UI changes minimal for sprint 27; prioritize features that unblock demos / sales.
- Avoid big refactors here — schedule for Optimize/Console overhaul in Q1.
- When closing tickets, always leave a one-line explanation and link to alternative epic if exists.

Attachments to add to ticket comments:
- simple-wireframe-route-row.png (mobile+desktop)
- model-selection-modal-sketch.png
- spike-brief-rollout-slider.md

End of doc.
